Definition.Name: Architecture decision governance and ADR stewardship
Definition.Summary: Guide architecture decisions from intake through option analysis, governance review, approval, and downstream rollout guidance without losing domain accountability or reusable evidence.
Definition.ValueStatement: Improve decision quality and prevent repeated architectural churn by forcing explicit options, trade-offs, approval reasoning, and follow-up obligations into durable ADR-style records.
Definition.InterfaceContractSummary: Decision demand, domain context, system constraints, and change risks are transformed into a reviewable architecture decision record with named owners and adoption conditions.
Definition.GovernanceNotes: Architecture decisions are treated as operating contracts, not slideware. The process requires evidence, option comparison, and explicit domain-owner participation.
Definition.ChangeSummary: Merged from SAMM governance, SSDF preparation and design, and lightweight ADR discipline so the process stays reusable across product, platform, and AI-oriented decisions.
Definition.GovernancePolicySummary: No architecture decision may be accepted without explicit context, considered options, decision rationale, risk notes, and named adoption obligations.
Definition.ConstitutionRuleSummary: The board may delay decisions, but cannot hide uncertainty by approving vague direction that nobody owns.
Definition.OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with human approval. Analysis may be AI-assisted, but acceptance and organizational commitment stay human.
Definition.SimulationReadinessSummary: Good fit for decision-board rehearsal, architecture review automation, and portfolio-level consistency analysis.

Roles.Purpose: Keep architecture governance lightweight but rigorous by ensuring the right decision, evidence, and follow-up happen at the right time.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A governance-capable facilitator who understands enough architecture to structure the process without dominating the decision.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Facilitator for architecture decision workflow discipline, records, and follow-through.

Roles.Purpose: Represent domain semantics, operational realities, and long-term consequences when architecture choices affect a specific capability area.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A leader who understands the domain model deeply enough to challenge superficially convenient architecture decisions.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Business-technical steward for a bounded domain affected by architectural change.

Roles.Purpose: Protect maintainability and operability by reviewing design options, target architecture fit, and downstream integration impact before costly implementation commitment.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior technical authority who can reason across components, environments, data boundaries, and operational consequences.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Architecture authority for system boundaries, irreversible decisions, and cross-domain technical coherence.

Roles.Purpose: Convert business intent into an explicit delivery contract with clear acceptance boundaries and prioritized value trade-offs.
Roles.StaffingIntent: One accountable human decision-maker who can clarify scope, decide priority, accept delivered outcomes, and absorb stakeholder escalation without routing every decision through engineering.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Outcome and acceptance owner for value, scope, sequencing, and release acceptance.

Roles.Purpose: Ensure changes touching trust boundaries, sensitive data, dependencies, or operational attack surface are reviewed proportionally and documented defensibly.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior security practitioner who can translate security risk into concrete engineering and governance decisions.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Security gate owner for threat assessment, exception handling, and trust-boundary decisions.

Roles.Purpose: Ensure required compliance considerations are identified early, translated into actionable checks, and retained as evidence.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A governance specialist who understands how policy obligations intersect with real delivery work.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Policy and evidence steward for contractual, regulatory, license, and audit-sensitive change decisions.

Roles.Purpose: Represent live-service constraints, operational history, and post-release accountability in change decisions.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A domain-aligned owner with authority over service-level objectives, support load, and operational trade-offs.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Operational accountability owner for a live service, product surface, or bounded business capability.

Steps.Title: Capture architecture decision demand
Steps.Subtitle: Define the decision boundary and why now
Steps.Notes: Normalize the incoming design tension into a single decision problem statement with scope, urgency, and impacted domains.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Design concern, change proposal, incident learning, or product demand requiring architecture direction.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Typed decision intake with named context owner and impacted domains.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Decision intake brief and initial affected-system list.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Governance facilitator may reject vague requests that do not define a real decision.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not proceed when scope and affected domains are not explicit.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Facilitation remains with trained board coordinator.
A domain owner must review the intake boundary.

Steps.Title: Assemble context, constraints, and options
Steps.Subtitle: Evidence before preference
Steps.Notes: Collect current-state constraints, target outcomes, option set, and measurable trade-offs before the board debates a preferred answer.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Decision intake, current system context, risk drivers, and domain constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: ADR draft with options, trade-offs, and recommendation.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Draft ADR and supporting context evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Solution architect authors the option analysis; domain owner confirms local reality and adoption cost.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If fewer than two meaningful options are considered, explain why explicitly.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Product value trade-offs are reviewed before board discussion.

Steps.Title: Review security, compliance, and policy impact
Steps.Subtitle: Decision quality includes control impact
Steps.Notes: Evaluate whether the proposed options change data exposure, trust assumptions, regulatory boundaries, or operational policy obligations.
Steps.InputContractSummary: ADR draft, system context, data flows, control inventory, and third-party implications.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Review note covering security and policy implications.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security and compliance findings tied to decision options.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer and compliance steward may force rework when controls are under-specified.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No approval when control obligations are ambiguous.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Compliance review becomes required for regulated domains.
Service owner reviews operational control impact.

Steps.Title: Make the board decision and record rationale
Steps.Subtitle: Approval is a commitment, not just agreement
Steps.Notes: Approve, defer, or reject the recommended architecture direction with explicit rationale, dissent notes, and adoption conditions.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Reviewed ADR draft, option analysis, and security/compliance notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or deferred architecture decision with adoption conditions.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Board decision record and named follow-up obligations.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Governance facilitator records the decision; service owner and domain owner must both acknowledge adoption obligations.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not approve with placeholders for ownership or decision rationale.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Approved
BranchOutcomes.Description: The ADR is accepted with adoption conditions.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Deferred
BranchOutcomes.Description: The ADR requires more evidence or narrower scope.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Operational decision approval remains with accountable owner.

Steps.Title: Publish rollout guidance and revisit triggers
Steps.Subtitle: Translate decision into executable downstream expectations
Steps.Notes: Turn the approved ADR into rollout guidance, architectural guardrails, and explicit revisit triggers so implementation teams know how to apply the decision.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Published rollout guidance and revisit criteria.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Architecture guidance note and future revisit triggers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Solution architect owns technical guidance; governance facilitator ensures revisit criteria are durable.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If rollout expectations cannot be stated clearly, the decision is not ready for downstream implementation.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture guidance ownership remains with the architect.

Warnings: Detailed sidecar metadata remains in the process-template pack files.
